usage: Pick a username and challenge it in the given format, e.g. '/challenge MM-Kakuna, gen9ou'. Every player accepts challenges from anyone and plays until it loses/forfeits or the battle ends. RL players load their checkpoint on the first challenge they receive.

players.description: Best public metamon policy (Dec 2025). Superkazam finetuned on 7.8M additional high-temperature self-play battles.
players.strength: Gen9OU GXE ~71% vs humans with sample teams (paper Table 1).

players.description: PokéAgent Challenge organizer baseline; played as PAC-MM-Wildcard / PAC-MM-Mystery during qualification.
players.strength: Gen9OU GXE ~64% vs humans; would have been #3 seed in the Gen9OU qualifier.

players.description: Final Kadabra trained on the full 11.6M self-play + parsed-replays-v4 corpus.
players.strength: #2 Gen9OU seed behind FoulPlay if it had been public; stronger than Kadabra3 on diverse teams.

players.description: Last model of the PokéAgent Challenge effort; Kadabra4 finetuned on a dataset patched for tera-type visibility.
players.strength: Slightly better than Kadabra3/4 on the current (patched) server, more robust across diverse teams.

players.description: Best publicly available Gen9OU agent during the NeurIPS 2025 PokéAgent Challenge; the basis of many third-party submissions.
players.strength: Gen9OU GXE ~50% vs humans with sample teams.

players.description: Revisits the PokéAgent Challenge dataset at ~142M parameters (11.6M self-play + 4M human battles).
players.strength: Between the 57M Kadabra line and Kakuna.

players.description: Mid-challenge policy; played on the ladder as PAC-MM-Alakazam.
players.strength: Held the top organizer Gen9OU rank at the end of the summer 2025 practice ladder.

players.description: Early PokéAgent Challenge self-play policy (gens 1-4 and 9).
players.strength: Held the top organizer Gen9OU rank for most of the summer 2025 practice ladder.

players.description: Tiny RNN trained on parsed-replays-v4 plus ~5M self-play battles; a cheap starting point for finetuning.
players.strength: Weakest of the modern RL policies, but cheap to run on CPU.

players.description: First Gen9-compatible prototype; trained only on human replays (parsed-replays v3).
players.strength: Roughly LargeRL-level in gens 1-4, weakest Gen9OU policy in the pool.

players.description: Uniformly picks a legal move (or switch). Measures the floor of the pool.
players.strength: Very weak; sanity-check opponent.

players.description: Actively bad trainer: always picks the least damaging move and the worst type matchup when forced to switch.
players.strength: Very weak; sanity-check opponent.

players.description: Usually picks the available move with the highest base power (10% random).
players.strength: Weak; no type or stat awareness.

players.description: Gen-1-flavoured trainer: random moves, first available switch when forced.
players.strength: Weak.

players.description: Gen1Trainer with type/speed-aware switching when forced to switch.
players.strength: Weak.

players.description: Emulates the Gen 1 'Good AI': random moves, but prefers stat boosts on the first turn and super-effective moves.
players.strength: Weak; Gen 1 logic applied to Gen 9.

players.description: Greedy damage dealer that switches on bad type matchups.
players.strength: Low.

players.description: Maximally offensive: picks the highest estimated damage move using the damage formula and type chart; best type matchup when switching.
players.strength: Moderate-low; no status/boosting play.

players.description: Grunt plus health awareness: boosts when healthy, heals when low.
players.strength: Moderate-low; a step above Grunt.

players.description: Grunt with Smogon-style switching heuristics.
players.strength: Moderate-low.

players.description: Small RNN imitation-learning policy trained on an early parsed-replay dataset; CPU inference.
players.strength: Low; pre-Gen9 IL checkpoint.

players.description: BaseRNN variant trained only on human wins.
players.strength: Low; pre-Gen9 IL checkpoint.

players.description: Smaller RNN imitation-learning baseline.
players.strength: Low; pre-Gen9 IL checkpoint.

players.description: Extended version of the Emerald Kaizo ROM-hack AI with additional rules.
players.strength: Moderate; large handwritten ruleset.

players.description: Port of the AI from the Pokémon Emerald Kaizo ROM hack: scores every option with a large handwritten ruleset.
players.strength: Moderate; the strongest heuristic baseline in the paper's composite.

players.description: The SimpleHeuristicsPlayer shipped with poke-env (type/damage heuristics).
players.strength: Moderate-low; the standard poke-env baseline.
